To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BDNF and dBcAMP rapidly differentiate the RN46A serotonin cell line towards a neuronal phenotype, but without changing the distribution of 2 serotonin autoreceptor subtypes.
BDNF and dBcAMP induce a neuronal-like phenotype in RN46A cells, but without the typical somato-dendritically targeted distribution of the 5HT(1) autreceptors.
BDNF- or dBcAMP-treated RN46A cells, which are differentiated towards a serotoninergic-like phenotype, do not display the somato-dendrite targeting of 5HT1A and 1B autoreceptor subtypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms of 5-HT autoreceptor targeting to somas and/or dendrites.
the molecular mechanisms of neuronal differentiation in the brain, and the development and maintenance of serotoninergic neurons in the brain.
the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of the serotonergic system in the raphe nuclei, which are the major source of serotonin in the brain and the main target for antidepressant drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 5-HT1 receptors, both 5-HT1a and 5-HT 1b receptors, are present in the soma and dendrites of the neurons.
5-HT(2A) receptors are located on the cell membrane and that 5-HT1 receptors are located in the cytosol.
the 5-HT1 autoreceptor distribution is not a function of neuronal differentiation but of neuronal maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RN46A cell line can differentiate into a neuron-like cell with serotonin immunopositive and Map2 positive, but the 5-HT1a and 5-HT 1b autoreceptors remain in the soma and dendrite, respectively.
BDNF and dBcAMP differentiate RN46A towards a neuronal serotonin-like phenotype without the differential distribution of 5HT(1A) or 5HT(2) autoreceptors.
the 5-HT1 autoreceptors are not differentially targeted by the BDNF and dBcAMP-induced differentiation of RN46A cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

RN46A cells are an interesting tool to study the molecular mechanism of the differential targeting of 5HT1A and 1B autoreceptor in neurons, and that this differential targeting is not a consequence of the neuronal differentiation.

the RN46A cells can be differentiated into neurons with a neuronal-like phenotype, which can be used to study the molecular mechanism of the somato-dendritically restricted distribution of the serotonin autoreceptors.
the RN46A cell line is a useful model for the study of 5-HT receptors, as well as the molecular mechanisms of neuronal development and plasticity.
